draft.title: Time zones
card: The world is divided into time zones. Each zone keeps its own clock time, so it can be morning in one country and night in another.
Zones are measured from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). A zone written UTC+3 is 3 hours ahead of UTC. A zone written UTC−5 is 5 hours behind UTC.
Sydney is UTC+10. During daylight saving, when clocks go forward 1 hour, Sydney is UTC+11.
To compare two places, find the gap between their UTC numbers. Example: UTC+10 and UTC+3 are 10 − 3 = 7 hours apart, and the higher number is ahead.
draft.remember: UTC+ means ahead of UTC and UTC− means behind. Sydney is UTC+10, or UTC+11 in daylight saving.

a.q: A city is in the UTC−5 time zone. How does its clock time compare with UTC?
opts: It is 5 hours ahead of UTC
It is the same as UTC
a.why: A minus sign means the zone is behind UTC, so UTC−5 is 5 hours behind. Reading it as ahead mixes up the sign, and the number counts hours, not minutes.
a.clue: Does the minus sign mean ahead or behind?

b.q: It is 2:00 pm in Sydney during daylight saving (UTC+11). What is the time at UTC+3?
b.why: UTC+11 and UTC+3 are 11 − 3 = 8 hours apart. UTC+3 is behind Sydney, so subtract 8 hours from 2:00 pm to get 6:00 am. Adding 8 hours gives 10:00 pm, which would put UTC+3 ahead of Sydney.
b.clue: Which zone has the higher number, and so is ahead?
